govdocs-archive_org-the-communist-party-: An FBI report in file HQ-116395, released under the Freedom of Information Act, examines the Communist Party USA and what the era called the Negro question. It records the party's stated position on Black Americans, as the bureau tracked it. The FBI watched the party for decades, and race was one of its constant concerns. The report shows both the party's line and the bureau's habits of watching it.
nasa-tm-19680018186-a-review-of-faciliti:
Seth B. Anderson and Laurel G. Schroers of Ames Research Center review low-speed flight test facilities and techniques in this paper. New classes of aircraft demand new and improved ways to test at low speed. Building novel aircraft is costly, so test methods must be trustworthy before full flight.

The authors survey the facilities available for low-speed work and the techniques used in them. They consider what new aircraft types require from those facilities. Gaps between current practice and future needs guide their review. The paper helps planners decide where to invest in test capability. It also helps engineers choose the right facility for a given low-speed program.
nasa-tm-19720019866-research-achievement:
Research Achievements Review, Volume 4, was issued May 30, 1972, as NASA TM X-64666. It covers quality and reliability assurance research at the Marshall Space Flight Center. The center's Science and Engineering Directorate published the review. Its theme, per the catalog record, is newer approaches to reliability engineering and quality control for aerospace work.

The contents open with two imaging studies. One develops solid-state radiographic X-ray image amplifiers, panels that make X-ray pictures without film. Tables and figures compare those panels with fluoroscopes and show images of a luggage interior and the inner fixture of a graphite-epoxy strut. A second study presents a neutron-radiation imaging system, with its own comparison tables. Together they show Marshall's quality researchers building better ways to inspect hardware without taking it apart.
